Brett Busby

Republican candidate for Supreme Court, Place 8, Texas

Justice, Supreme Court of Texas, Place 8 (incumbent)

Brett Busby is a Republican justice on the Supreme Court of Texas, Place 8. Gov. Greg Abbott appointed him in 2019, and he was elected to the seat in 2020, defeating Democrat Gisela Triana. He was unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and faces Triana again in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Busby stands

Judicial independence
Says he is "not on a team" as a judge. His campaign presents this as a commitment to judicial independence.
Access to legal services
Oversees the Texas Access to Justice Commission. His campaign highlights his work to expand access to legal help for people who cannot afford lawyers.
Qualifications
Points to his experience as a board-certified appellate lawyer and his record as a judge. Notes that the Texas Senate voted unanimously to confirm his Supreme Court appointment.

Background

  • Justice, Supreme Court of Texas, Place 8, 2019–present (appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott; elected 2020)
  • Justice, Texas 14th Court of Appeals (Houston), Place 3, 2012–2018
  • Appellate lawyer; former partner at Bracewell LLP
  • Former law clerk at the U.S. Supreme Court and the U.S. 11th Circuit Court of Appeals
  • B.A., Duke University; J.D., Columbia Law School
  • Unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary (1,719,374 votes)
